Commentary.Commentary: So after a breathtaking victory, Zimbabwe stay alive in the series and make it 1-2! It will take some time for the hosts to let this victory soak in but they don't have time for it as the next game takes place in three day's time. And that too being a do-or-die contest for them in the series. The visitors on the other hand would be frustrated with their today's performance and will look to bounce back hard in the next game which takes place at Harare Sports Club on 24th February at 0930 local time (0730 GMT).

The Man of the Match award has been awarded to Tendai Chatara as well as Sean Williams. The former begin the proceedings with the ball and ended with the figures of 10-0-30-3! Whereas Sean Williams triggered the collapse by picking wickets of Gulbadin Naib, Mohammad Nabi and Amir Hamza in the end.

After a poor effort with the bat, the Chefrons were superb with the ball. They kept on picking wickets at regular intervals which proved to be the undoing of the visitors. Tendai Chatara started the proceedings as he bowled his full quota of 10 overs on trot in the start and scalped 3 wickets, giving away just 30 runs. And in the end it was Sean Williams and Chris Mpofu who scripted Zimbabwe's way to victory by picking up 3 wickets apiece in quick succession.

Then there was a twist in tale! Sean Williams and Chris Mpofu had other things in mind and started the collapse similar to the way their team collapsed in the first innings. Mpofu first sent Shenwari and Najibullah packing in back-to-back deliveries. Then pressure got better of Nabi while the remaining task proved too much for the tail. In first innings, Zimbabwe were restricted from 121/5 to 129 all out while Afghanistan bundled out from 121/5 to 126 all out. The last three runs scored in the first innings proved to be the difference in the end.

After losing 3 quick wickets, Asghar Stanikzai and Samiullah Shenwari calmed things down for the visitors and looked set on the path towards victory. After the skipper's departure Gulbadin Naib walked in and added 33 runs for 5th wicket before getting out to a rather loose shot. Still the visitors were the clear favourites as they needed just 23 runs with 5 wickets in hand. And with Shenwari and Nabi out in the middle it looked like a stroll in the park for the Afghans.

What a victory! Zimbabwe have pulled out a thriller! Cricket is a game of glorious uncertainties and today's match was one of the best example of it. With just 130 needed to win the match and the series, the visitors were the clear favourites. However, it wasn't to be. The hosts started in a great fashion as they got rid of Noor Ali in the second over itself and then also got the precious wicket of Shahzad as he looked to take the attack to them.

OUT c Peter Moor b Chris Mpofu. Afghanistan have lost their ninth wicket.
OUT b Sean Williams. Afghanistan have lost their eighth wicket.
OUT c Peter Moor b Chris Mpofu. Afghanistan have lost their seventh wicket.
OUT c Peter Moor b Chris Mpofu. Afghanistan have lost their sixth wicket.

After 25 overs, Afghanistan take a step closer to victory as they move to 111/5! As Afghanistan were closing on the win, they lost another wicket in Gulbadin Naib. Sean Williams was the one who took the wicket but it didn't change much in the context of the game. Samiullah Shenwari is still out there and will look to stay till the end and see his team through. AFGHANISTAN ARE JUST 19 RUNS SHY OF A SERIES WIN!
OUT c & b Sean Williams. Afghanistan have lost their fifth wicket.

After 20 overs, Afghanistan are 91/4! After the break, Zimbabwean bowlers were more disciplined. They didn't leak easy runs and in the process of getting to target quickly, Stanikzai edged one to Moor. Tendai Chatara bowled out his quota of 10 overs on trot and ended with a superb figures of 10-0-30-3! Gulbadin Naib has walked out in the middle and with Shenwari is approaching the target cautiously. Afghanistan now NEED 39 RUNS MORE TO WIN!
OUT c Peter Moor b Tendai Chatara. Afghanistan have lost their fourth wicket.

Players are back after the break. The skipper, Stanikzai and Shenwari look set to take their team across the finish line as THEY REQUIRE JUST 67 RUNS MORE TO WIN! Greame Cremer in his second over will start the proceedings after the break with the ball.

After 13 overs, Afghanistan move to 63/3! The visitors found themselves three down soon when Tendai Chatara got rid of Rahmat Shah, to pick his second of the match. But, it happened to be just a mere hiccup as the skipper then took things under his control and started scoring at a strike rate of more than run-a-ball. Shenwari has now joined the skipper in the middle and are amidst an unbeaten 24-run partnership. Apart from Chatara, no other bowler is looking even a little threatening. It looks as if it just a matter of time when the visiting side crosses the line and win the series. As the first innings ended early, LUNCH BREAK has been taken now! We will resume shortly, stay tuned for the further updates!
OUT c Solomon Mire b Tendai Chatara. Afghanistan have lost their third wicket.

After 5 overs, Afghanistan have marched on to 27/2! In the second over itself, Afghanistan lost their first wicket as Ngarva bagged Noor Ali for a golden duck. Mohammad Shahzad then started to attack and quickly moved to 20. But then Shahzad went for one shot too many and ended up mistiming one to Musakanda at deep mid-wicket. Now the skipper has walked in to join Rahmat Shah. They require 103 runs more to win!
OUT c Tarisai Musakanda b Tendai Chatara. Afghanistan have lost their second wicket.
OUT c Graeme Cremer b Richard Ngarava. Afghanistan have lost their first wicket.

We are back for the chase. Mohammad Shahzad and Noor Ali Zadran to open the batting. They just need 130 runs for the series win. Tendai Chatara to begin the proceedings with the ball. Can they scalp some early wickets and put the visitors under pressure?
